steps: The sheet metal is sheared on a Shear (Sheet Metal) machine using a high-speed steel blade with tungsten carbide edge at a shear angle of 2 degrees and a cutting speed of 30 meters per minute, transforming it into sheared sheet metal, and the operation runs for 83 minutes.

A metal bar is loaded on a mobile robot and undergoes rough turning on a horizontal lathe using a carbide insert tool (CNMG 432) at a spindle speed of 450 RPM and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part, all for 59 minutes.

On the Punch Press, a punching operation is performed on sheet metal for 49 minutes, using a 12 mm diameter punch at a stroke speed of 80 strokes per minute with automatic die alignment via optical sensor, transforming the input sheet metal on the conveyor belt into a finished cut sheet metal product that remains on the conveyor belt.

On the Stewart Platform Mills, precision milling is performed on the milled part to achieve a high-accuracy finish with a milling precision of ±0.005 mm, using a 6-axis adaptive toolpath with diamond-coated end mill and active hydraulic dampers engaged for vibration control, resulting in a ground part, and the operation runs for 84 minutes with the component loaded via MobileRobot.

On a Broaching Machine, an internal broaching operation is performed on a lathed part using a pull-type internal broach with 18 teeth at a feed rate of 1.2 mm/stroke to achieve a Class 6 fit, processing for 35 minutes, resulting in a broached component that is placed in the MobileRobot.

On a Screw Machines, a Thread Rolling operation is performed on a Lathed part loaded in a MobileRobot, producing a Screwed component, using an M12 x 1.75 metric coarse thread with a production rate of 120 units per hour, and the operation runs for 68 minutes.

Using a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine), a ground part is wire cut in a fine finish with multi-pass skim cut mode and automatic edge polishing enabled for deburring, using deionized water with conductivity less than 5 μS/cm as the dielectric fluid, resulting in a precision finished part, all processed for 58 minutes with both the input and output components held in a MobileRobot.

On a Vertical Lathe, the drilled component is machined using facing and turning operations with CNC-controlled contouring and radial infeed at a rotation speed of 320 RPM and a precision level of ±0.01 mm tolerance, resulting in a final drilled and shaped part, taking 66 minutes.

On a Bandsaw, a metal bar is cut into a lathed part through a bar cutting operation that lasts for 44 minutes, using a bi-metal variable pitch blade with 4 TPI at a saw speed of 60 meters per minute and producing a 3 mm kerf width.
The milled part is surface planed on a planer for 2 minutes, achieving a surface finish of Ra 3.2 μm with a planing depth of 0.5 mm per pass and a feed rate of 1.8 m/min, resulting in a planed part.

On a CNC Turning Center, a finish turning operation is performed on a lathed part loaded in a MobileRobot, using CNC program #7A to finish the contour with a taper and chamfer at a spindle speed of 600 RPM and tool offsets of X: 0.02 mm and Z: 0.01 mm, resulting in a finished machined component, all for 63 minutes.

On the Gear Shaper machine, a broached component is shaped into a spur gear with 32 teeth through the gear shaping operation at a speed of 180 strokes per minute, resulting in a shaped gear, and this process takes 25 minutes.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on a sheet metal component placed on the conveyor belt, using a 3000-watt laser with nitrogen gas assist at 18 bar for clean edge quality and a cutting speed of 4.5 m/min, transforming the input into cut sheet metal and completing the operation in 70 minutes.

Using a Drill Press, a precision drilling operation is performed on the broached component for 1 minute, creating holes with a diameter of 8.5 mm at a tolerance of ±0.05 mm and a spindle speed of 1100 RPM, resulting in a finished part with holes.

Using a grinding machine, perform surface grinding on the planed part loaded in the mobile robot for 84 minutes with an aluminum oxide grinding wheel of 60 grit at a wheel speed of 1800 m/min and a feed rate of 0.005 mm/pass, resulting in a ground part that remains in the mobile robot.

On a Hobbing Machine, gear hobbing is performed on a broached component to create an involute gear profile with a 20-degree pressure angle, operating at a hobbing speed of 120 RPM and a feed rate of 2.5 mm/rev, resulting in a hobbied gear, all for 56 minutes, with both the input broached component and the output hobbied gear handled by a MobileRobot.

On a vertical milling machine, perform profile milling on a cut sheet metal component using a carbide end mill with a 10 mm diameter, following a climb milling pattern with a closed-loop contour to achieve a tolerance of ±0.1 mm, resulting in a finished sheet metal product, all within a processing duration of 35 minutes.

On the Honing Machine, the Cylinder Honing operation is performed on the Honed cylinder to achieve a precision finish, using a honing grit size of 220 mesh and targeting a bore size of 50.025 mm ± 0.005 mm, lasting for 46 minutes, resulting in a Precision finished part, all while the component remains in the MobileRobot.

On a Shaper, a Keyway Shaping operation is performed on a Milled part loaded in a MobileRobot for 81 minutes using a high-speed steel single-point cutter at a shaping speed of 30 strokes per minute and a stroke length of 120 mm, resulting in a Shaped part that remains in the MobileRobot.

Using a horizontal milling machine, face milling is performed on the milled part to achieve a flat surface with a crosshatch tool path pattern, operating at a milling speed of 220 RPM and achieving a surface finish of Ra 1.6 μm, resulting in a finished machined component, all for 58 minutes.

Using a broaching machine, a lathed part is broached with a pull-type broach at a high precision level, transforming it into a broached component, which is then placed on a conveyor belt, and the operation takes 11 minutes.

The milled part is planed on a Planer for 67 minutes, achieving a planing depth of 2.5 mm, a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, and a surface finish of Ra 3.2 µm, resulting in a planed part that is transferred to a MobileRobot.

A metal bar is loaded from a mobile robot into a horizontal lathe where it undergoes rough turning for 45 minutes at a rotation speed of 800 rpm and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev using a carbide insert tool, resulting in a lathed part that is unloaded onto a conveyor belt.

Using a Drill Press, a precision drilling operation is performed on the broached component located on the ConveyorBelt to create holes with a diameter of 10 mm and a tolerance of +/- 0.05 mm, taking 86 minutes to complete, resulting in a finished part with holes that is then transferred to the MobileRobot as a DrilledComponent.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) machine performs a shearing operation on sheet metal, cutting it into sheared sheet metal using a high-carbon steel blade at a shear angle of 1.5 degrees and a cutting speed of 20 mm/s, taking 91 minutes to complete, with the input material delivered by a MobileRobot and the output placed on a ConveyorBelt.

The planed part is subjected to surface grinding on a grinding machine using an aluminum oxide grinding wheel rotating at 3500 rpm with a feed rate of 0.1 mm/pass, lasting for 60 minutes, resulting in a ground part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

On the Vertical Lathe, a finish turning operation is performed on the drilled component using a CNC-controlled contouring toolpath with high precision, transforming it into the final drilled and shaped part, which is then placed on the mobile robot, and the process takes 61 minutes.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on sheet metal for 6 minutes, using a laser power of 2500 W, a cutting speed of 2.5 m/min, and nitrogen as the gas assist, resulting in cut sheet metal that is transferred to the conveyor belt.

Using a screw machine, automatic screw machining is performed on a lathed part to produce a screwed component with an M10 metric coarse thread, running for 95 minutes at a production rate of 120 parts per hour, after which the finished component is placed on a conveyor belt.

On the Honing Machine, a honing operation is performed on the Honed cylinder to achieve precise bore finishing, using a honing grit size of 220 to reach a bore size of 50 mm, and the process runs for 18 minutes, resulting in a Precision finished part that is transferred to the MobileRobot.

Using a Bandsaw, cold sawing is performed on a metal bar loaded from a MobileRobot, operating at a saw speed of 60 rpm with a bi-metal blade and a cutting width of 3 mm, taking 7 minutes to produce a lathed part that is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

The punch press performs a punching operation on a sheet metal component, using a 15 mm punch at a stroke speed of 80 strokes per minute with automatic die alignment, processing the material for 73 minutes to produce a finished sheet metal product that is then transferred to a conveyor belt.

A cut sheet metal component is precision milled using perimeter contouring on a vertical milling machine for 3 minutes, achieving a tolerance of +/- 0.1 mm, resulting in a finished sheet metal product that is transferred to a mobile robot.

On the CNC Turning Center, a CNC turning operation is performed on a lathed part for 92 minutes, using CNC program Program_003 with verified and loaded tool offsets and a spindle speed of 1200 rpm, resulting in a finished machined component that is transferred to the conveyor belt.

A milled part is machined using multi-axis milling on a Stewart Platform Mills for 30 minutes, achieving high milling precision with a 6-axis synchronized tool configuration and an active damping system to minimize vibrations, resulting in a ground part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

The milled part is shaped on a Shaper using an HSS cutting tool with a stroke length of 300 mm and a shaping speed of 20 strokes per minute, resulting in a shaped part, and the operation runs for 93 minutes before the output is placed on a ConveyorBelt.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs wire EDM cutting on the ground part using deionized water as the dielectric fluid in fine finish mode with deburring enabled, taking 7 minutes to produce a precision finished part that is then transferred to the mobile robot.

The Horizontal Milling Machine performs a horizontal milling operation using face milling as the tool path at a milling speed of 1000 rpm to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, processing the milled part for 37 minutes, which is delivered by the MobileRobot and results in a finished machined component transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

On the Gear Shaper machine, a broached component is shaped into a spur gear with 24 teeth through the gear shaping operation at a shaping speed of 60 rpm, taking 14 minutes, after which the resulting shaped gear is transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Hobbing Machine, a gear hobbing operation is performed on a broached component for 9 minutes, using a hobbing speed of 150 rpm and a feed rate of 0.5 mm/rev to produce an involute gear profile, resulting in a hobbied gear that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

The Stewart Platform Mills performs precision grinding on a milled part for 34 minutes, using a diamond-coated grinding tool with a milling precision of 5 microns and an active damping system engaged, transforming the input milled part carried by the MobileRobot into a ground part that is then placed on the ConveyorBelt.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on a sheet metal component located on the conveyor belt, using a laser power of 2500 watts, a cutting speed of 3 meters per minute, and nitrogen assist gas, taking 5 minutes to produce a cut sheet metal that is transferred to a mobile robot.

Perform finish milling on the milled part using a horizontal milling machine for 2 minutes at a milling speed of 1200 RPM, following a climb milling tool path with contouring to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 micrometers, resulting in a finished machined component transferred to the conveyor belt.

On the Honing Machine, a cylinder honing operation is performed on a honed cylinder to achieve precise bore finishing, using a 150 grit honing stone to reach a final bore size of 50.00 mm ± 0.01 mm, and the process runs for 26 minutes, after which the precision finished part is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

On the Bandsaw machine, a metal bar is cut into a lathed part through a bar cutting operation that runs for 55 minutes, using a bi-metal variable tooth blade with a saw speed of 60 meters per minute and producing a 3 mm kerf, after which the resulting lathed part is placed on a mobile robot.

A lathed part is subjected to roughing milling on a vertical milling machine for 24 minutes using a carbide end mill at a milling speed of 800 RPM and a depth of cut of 5 mm, resulting in a milled part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

On a Screw Machines, thread rolling is performed on a lathed part to create a metric coarse thread of size M10, operating at a production rate of 120 parts per hour, taking 28 minutes to complete, after which the resulting screwed component is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

On a Horizontal Lathe, a metal bar is subjected to rough turning for 3 minutes, using a carbide insert TNMG tool at a spindle speed of 450 RPM and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part that is then placed on a conveyor belt.

The Horizontal Milling Machine performs finish milling on the Rough Milled Part, using a climb milling tool path with contour following at a milling speed of 1200 RPM to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, resulting in the Finished Machined Component, and the operation takes 90 minutes before the part is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

The Laser Cutter performs laser cutting on a Stainless Steel Sheet, using 4000 W laser power, a cutting speed of 15 m/min, and nitrogen gas assist at 20 bar, for 4 minutes, transforming the input into a Laser Cut Sheet Metal that is then placed on a ConveyorBelt.

On a Hobbing Machine, gear hobbing is performed on a Broached Gear Blank to produce a Hobbed Spur Gear with an involute profile, 20° pressure angle, and 32 teeth, using a hobbing speed of 600 RPM and a feed rate of 0.5 mm/rev, lasting for 70 minutes, after which the component is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

On a CNC Turning Center, a precision turning operation is performed on a pre-turned shaft loaded from a mobile robot, using CNC program #SHAFT-02 with tool offsets verified and loaded for tools T01–T04 and a spindle speed of 850 RPM, resulting in a precision turned shaft that is transferred to a conveyor belt after processing for 36 minutes.

Using a bandsaw, a bar cutting operation is performed on an alloy steel bar stock loaded from a mobile robot, cutting it to length at a saw speed of 80 RPM with a bi-metal blade of 4/6 TPI and a cutting width of 3.2 mm, producing a cut-to-length shaft blank that is transferred to a conveyor belt, and the process takes 46 minutes.

Using a drill press, a steel bar with a keyway is drilled with a 12.7 mm drill bit at a spindle speed of 950 RPM and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, resulting in a drilled housing component, and the operation takes 78 minutes before the output is placed on a conveyor belt.

On the Gear Shaper, gear shaping is performed for 60 minutes to produce an internal spur gear with 40 teeth at a shaping speed of 180 strokes/min, starting from a Gear Blank with Internal Spline loaded by a MobileRobot and resulting in a ShapedGear component delivered to a ConveyorBelt.

On a Broaching Machine, a round metal bar is spline broached using a pull-type spline broach with a feed rate of 0.1 mm/tooth and a depth of cut of 4.5 mm, transforming it into a spline broached shaft, and this operation takes 67 minutes, after which the part is transferred to a conveyor belt.

A milled flat surface workpiece is shaped into a shaped guide rail using a shaper machine through a shaping operation with a stroke length of 300 mm, a shaping speed of 40 strokes/min, and an HSS single-point tool, lasting for 39 minutes, after which the resulting shaped part is placed on a conveyor belt.

On a Vertical Lathe, a Large Diameter Steel Disc is faced and turned using a carbide insert tool (CNMG 432) at a rotation speed of 320 RPM and a feed rate of 0.18 mm/rev for 71 minutes, resulting in a Turned Disc Component that is then placed on a ConveyorBelt.

On a Horizontal Lathe, a steel rod stock is turned into a cylindrical shaft through a turning operation running for 61 minutes, using a tungsten carbide round insert tool at a spindle speed of 750 RPM and a feed rate of 0.25 mm/rev, with the finished part placed on a conveyor belt.

The Stewart Platform Mills performs precision milling with active damping on the Milled Aerospace Bracket, using a 6-axis synchronized spindle and an active piezoelectric vibration damping system to achieve a milling precision of ±0.005 mm, processing the part for 75 minutes and resulting in a Precision Ground Surface that is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

On a Screw Machines, Screw Threading is performed on Turned Rod End components to create Threaded Connector parts, using an M10 screw size with a metric coarse thread of 1.5 pitch, running for 13 minutes at a production rate of 120 parts per hour, with input components delivered by MobileRobot and finished parts placed on a ConveyorBelt.

The surface grinding operation is performed on a grinding machine to achieve a precision ground surface, processing the planed guide way component loaded from a mobile robot using an aluminum oxide grinding wheel with 60 grit at a wheel speed of 1750 m/min and a feed rate of 0.05 mm/pass, lasting for 69 minutes, after which the resulting ground precision surface component is transferred to a conveyor belt.

On a Vertical Milling Machine, face and profile milling is performed on a Turned Flange for 76 minutes using a carbide end mill with a 16 mm diameter at a milling speed of 1100 RPM and a depth of cut of 3 mm, resulting in a Milled Flange with Keyseat that is placed on a ConveyorBelt.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) machine performs a shearing operation on a Cold Rolled Steel Sheet, cutting it into a Sheared Rectangular Blank using a hardened steel, straight edge blade with a shear angle of 1.5° and a cutting speed of 8 cuts per minute, and the process takes 4 minutes, after which the cut sheet metal is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

On the Punch Press, a flat sheet metal blank is punched using a 25 mm round punch at a stroke speed of 120 strokes per minute with laser-aligned die set to a tolerance of ±0.1 mm, transforming it into a punched bracket that is then placed on a conveyor belt, all taking 54 minutes.

The Honing Machine performs internal honing on a Bored Cylinder Liner, using a 220 mesh honing grit to achieve a bore size of 85.000 ±0.003 mm, resulting in a Precision Bore Cylinder, which is then transferred to a ConveyorBelt, all for 97 minutes.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs wire EDM cutting on the Shaped Die Insert, using a brass wire with a 0.25 mm diameter at a cutting speed of 8 mm/min and electrical parameters of 250 A peak current and 10 kHz frequency, resulting in a Precision EDM Cut Insert, and the operation runs for 29 minutes before the output part is placed on the ConveyorBelt.

The Planer performs surface planing on the Rough Milled Base Plate, which is loaded via MobileRobot, removing material to a depth of 2.5 mm with a feed rate of 0.3 mm/stroke to achieve a surface finish of Ra 3.2 µm, resulting in a Flat Planed Surface that is transferred to the ConveyorBelt, and the operation runs for 59 minutes.

steps: On the Punch Press, punching is performed on a sheet metal component located on the ConveyorBelt for 44 minutes, using a 25 mm punch at a stroke speed of 80 strokes per minute with automatic die alignment set to center-aligned, resulting in a punched sheet metal component classified as CutSheetMetal that remains on the ConveyorBelt.

On a Vertical Lathe, a metal bar is turned into a lathed part using a carbide insert tool (CNMG 432) at a rotation speed of 650 rpm and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, with the operation lasting for 89 minutes, after which the finished part remains on the MobileRobot.

Using a vertical milling machine, a lathed part is milled for 36 minutes with a 12 mm diameter HSS end mill at a milling speed of 1200 rpm and a depth of cut of 3 mm, resulting in a milled part that remains on the mobile robot.

On a Bandsaw, a metal bar is cut into a cut-off blank through a sawing operation lasting 25 minutes, using a bi-metal variable pitch blade with 4 TPI at a saw speed of 90 m/min and a cutting width of 0.5 mm kerf, with both the input metal bar and resulting cut-off blank transported via conveyor belt.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs wire EDM cutting on the shaped part loaded in the MobileRobot, using brass-coated steel wire with a diameter of 0.25 mm, electrical parameters of 120 V and 10 A, and a cutting speed of 8 mm/min, operating for 32 minutes to produce a precision finished part, which remains in the MobileRobot.

The milled part is planed on a planer for 77 minutes, achieving a planing depth of 1.5 mm, a feed rate of 300 mm/min, and a surface finish of Ra 3.2 µm, resulting in a planed part, with both the input and output components handled by a mobile robot.

On a Hobbing Machine, a gear hobbing operation is performed on a broached component to produce a hobbied gear with an involute profile, 20° pressure angle, and 36 teeth, running at a hobbing speed of 150 rpm and a feed rate of 1.2 mm/rev, and the process takes 72 minutes, after which the hobbied gear remains in the MobileRobot.

The honing machine performs a honing operation on the honed cylinder, using a 180 grit honing stone to achieve a bore size of 50.00 ± 0.01 mm, resulting in a precision finished cylinder, and this process runs for 39 minutes with the component loaded in the mobile robot.

Using a drill press, a metal bar is drilled with a 10 mm drill bit at a spindle speed of 750 rpm and a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev, transforming it into a drilled component, and this operation takes 58 minutes.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on a sheet metal component located on the conveyor belt for 49 minutes, using a laser power of 2500 W, a cutting speed of 2.5 m/min, and nitrogen gas assist at 12 bar, resulting in a cut sheet metal component that remains on the conveyor belt.

Using a CNC Turning Center, a lathed part is machined through a CNC Turning operation for 56 minutes, executing CNC program #1045 with verified and loaded tool offsets in the turret and a spindle speed of 850 rpm, resulting in a finished machined component, both the input and output being transported via MobileRobot.

On a Horizontal Lathe, a metal bar is turned into a lathed part using a carbide insert TNMG 16 tool at a rotation speed of 700 rpm and a feed rate of 0.18 mm/rev, with the operation lasting for 22 minutes and the part remaining on the conveyor belt throughout.

On a Screw Machines, screw threading is performed on a lathed part to create a metric coarse thread of size M12 x 1.75 at a production rate of 120 units per hour, resulting in a screwed component, and the operation runs for 46 minutes.

On the Gear Shaper machine, a broached component is shaped into a spur gear with 24 teeth through a gear shaping operation running at 110 rpm for 15 minutes, resulting in a shaped gear carried by the MobileRobot.

Using a horizontal milling machine, the milled part is subjected to a milling operation at a spindle speed of 1100 rpm with a climb milling and full slotting tool path to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, resulting in a finished machined component, and the process runs for 58 minutes.

The planed part is subjected to surface grinding using a grinding machine equipped with an aluminum oxide grinding wheel of 60 grit at a wheel speed of 1800 m/min and a feed rate of 250 mm/min, transforming it into a ground part, and this operation lasts for 53 minutes with both the input and output components transported by a mobile robot.

The sheet metal is sheared on a Shear (Sheet Metal) machine using a hardened steel straight-edge blade with a 2° shear angle and a cutting speed of one cut every 15 seconds, processing for 27 minutes to produce sheared sheet metal, which is conveyed on a conveyor belt.

A milled part is processed using multi-axis milling on a Stewart Platform Mills machine for 56 minutes, achieving a milling precision of ±0.005 mm with a 6-axis synchronized spindle and an active hydraulic damping system, resulting in a ground part that remains in the MobileRobot container.

On a broaching machine, a metal bar is broached using a pull-type keyway broach to create a keyway feature with a depth of cut of 5 mm in one pass at a feed rate of 5 mm depth, resulting in a broached component, and the operation takes 11 minutes.

On the Stewart Platform Mills, the milled part is transformed into a ground part through precision surface milling with vibration control for 25 minutes, using high-precision 5-axis contouring mode to achieve tight tolerances of ±0.001 mm, a carbide end mill with 4 flutes and a 12 mm diameter featuring center-cutting geometry, and an active damping system that utilizes real-time feedback from piezoelectric sensors to minimize vibrations, with the resulting ground part placed on a conveyor belt upon completion.

The Cold Sawing of Metal Bar Stock operation is performed on a Bandsaw for 66 minutes, using a bi-metal variable pitch blade with 6 TPI for smooth finish and chip removal, a saw speed of 60 meters per minute optimized for alloy steel cutting, and a kerf width of 1.2 mm to minimize material waste, transforming a Metal bar fed from a ConveyorBelt into a Lathed part loaded onto a MobileRobot.

Using a drill press, a center drilling operation is performed on a metal bar to prepare for subsequent machining, lasting for 4 minutes, with a 6 mm diameter high-speed steel twist drill having an 118° point angle, a spindle speed of 850 RPM to maintain optimal surface speed for carbon steel, and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev to ensure clean hole formation without burring, resulting in a drilled component that is placed on a conveyor belt.

The Laser Cutter performs high-power CO2 laser cutting on sheet metal, using 4000 W output power, a cutting speed of 2.5 meters per minute with dynamic acceleration control, and oxygen assist gas at 12 bar pressure to achieve clean cuts in 10 mm thick mild steel, resulting in cut sheet metal, and the operation takes 23 minutes, after which the MobileRobot transports the processed part.

The Fine Wire EDM Cutting with Deburring Function operation is performed on a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) for 78 minutes, using a multi-pass skim cut with reverse polarity to achieve a mirror finish and a final pass with a low-energy spark deburring cycle to remove micro-burrs, while maintaining deionized water as the dielectric fluid with conductivity below 10 μS/cm, starting with a ground part loaded from the MobileRobot and resulting in a precision finished part placed on the ConveyorBelt.

The milled part is subjected to surface planing for flatness correction on a planer for 29 minutes, using a carbide-tipped single-point tool with a planing depth of 0.5 mm per pass to achieve flatness within 0.01 mm over 300 mm and a feed rate of 150 mm/min synchronized with table reciprocation speed, resulting in a surface finish target of Ra 3.2 μm, producing a planed part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

Using a Punch Press, turret punching for panel features is performed on sheet metal for 16 minutes, employing a 25 mm round punch for mounting holes indexed from an automatic turret, a stroke speed of 300 strokes per minute with servo-controlled impact force, and a hydraulic self-aligning die set with automatic clearance adjustment, transforming the input sheet metal delivered by a MobileRobot into a finished sheet metal product that is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

On a Honing Machine, the Honed cylinder is subjected to Internal Cylindrical Honing for Bearing Surface for 69 minutes, using 180-grit aluminum oxide stones for the initial cut followed by 400-grit stones for the finish, achieving a final bore diameter of 50.025 mm with ±0.005 mm tolerance through a cycle that includes rough, finish, and plateau honing stages, resulting in a Precision finished part transferred to a MobileRobot.

On a Bar-Feed Lathe, an automatic screw threading operation is performed on lathed parts to create an external parallel thread with a 60° profile per ISO 68-1 standard, cutting an M12 x 1.75 mm metric thread in multiple passes at a production rate of 180 parts per hour with automatic cutoff and part ejection, processing the parts for 26 minutes, where the input consists of lathed parts delivered by a MobileRobot and the output consists of screwed components placed on a ConveyorBelt.

The planed part is subjected to surface grinding for dimensional accuracy using a grinding machine equipped with an aluminum oxide wheel of 36 grit, medium hardness, and vitrified bond, operating at a peripheral speed of 1600 m/min and a feed rate of 4.5 mm/stroke with an automatic infeed increment of 0.02 mm per pass, lasting for 68 minutes, resulting in a ground part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

Using a horizontal milling machine, perform heavy-duty face milling with indexable cutters on the milled part loaded from the mobile robot, operating at a spindle speed of 220 RPM with a 100 mm face mill for cutting tool steel, employing a climb milling strategy with helical entry to reduce tool wear and utilizing wiper insert geometry to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 μm, resulting in a finished machined component transferred to the conveyor belt, all for 95 minutes.

A milled part is machined on a shaper using linear shaping to create a keyway and slot, operating for 56 minutes with a high-speed steel single-point tool featuring a 15° rake angle for chip flow, a 150 mm adjustable stroke length to match feature requirements, and a shaping speed of 35 strokes per minute with the quick return mechanism engaged, resulting in a shaped part transferred to a mobile robot.

A metal bar is loaded onto a vertical lathe where it undergoes facing and turning operations on a vertical turning center for 31 minutes, using a carbide insert with TNMG 16 04 04 geometry and CVD coating at a rotation speed of 420 RPM adapted for an 80 mm diameter alloy steel workpiece and a feed rate of 0.18 mm/rev for balanced finish and productivity, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

On a CNC Turning Center, perform finish turning with live tooling on a lathed part for 10 minutes using CNC program #TC-2024-FIN executing G-code with tool compensation, a Z-axis tool offset of -0.012 mm to achieve final length tolerance, and a spindle speed of 1200 RPM with synthetic cutting oil, loading the part from a ConveyorBelt and unloading the finished machined component to a MobileRobot.

A metal bar is loaded onto a horizontal lathe where rough and finish turning operations are performed using a high-speed steel round-nose tool for roughing at 300 RPM and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev, followed by carbide tool finishing at the same spindle speed with the feed rate reduced to 0.1 mm/rev to minimize vibration on large-diameter stock, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a conveyor belt after processing for 83 minutes.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) performs guillotine shearing of a steel plate for 74 minutes, using hardened tool steel blades with a hardness of HRC 58-60 to ensure long edge life, a shear angle of 2.5° rake angle to reduce cutting force and distortion, and a cutting speed of a full stroke cycle time of 8 seconds including return, starting with sheet metal fed from a conveyor belt and resulting in sheared sheet metal transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Hobbing Machine, a broached component is machined for 3 minutes using gear hobbing to generate spur gear teeth with a hobbing speed of 180 RPM hob rotation synchronized with workpiece index and a feed rate of 5 mm/rev axial feed to achieve full tooth depth in one pass, producing a hobbied gear featuring a 20° pressure angle, 36 teeth, module 2.5, and full involute form, which is then placed on a ConveyorBelt.

On the Gear Shaper, an internal gear shaping operation is performed on a broached component loaded from a conveyor belt, using a single-thread cutter at 220 strokes per minute with automatic backlash compensation to produce a 40-tooth internal spur gear with a 3 mm module via the generating method, resulting in a shaped gear transferred to a mobile robot, and the process runs for 8 minutes.

On a Broaching Machine, perform internal pull broaching for keyway formation on a lathed part using a pull-type broach with 12 incremental cutting teeth and chip breakers to achieve a keyway width of 10H7 with ±0.015 mm tolerance by removing 1.8 mm of material in a single continuous stroke, taking 24 minutes, where the input lathed part is loaded via MobileRobot and the resulting broached component is transferred to a ConveyorBelt upon completion.

On a Vertical Milling Machine, perform perimeter milling and deburring of a laser-cut panel for 68 minutes, using a 10 mm diameter ball nose end mill with TiAlN coating for edge durability, following a climb milling pattern along the outer contour with corner radius compensation while maintaining dimensional accuracy within ±0.05 mm over 500 mm length, starting with cut sheet metal on a conveyor belt and resulting in a finished sheet metal product loaded onto a mobile robot.

A lathed part is subjected to roughing milling on a vertical milling machine for 19 minutes, using a carbide end mill with a 12mm diameter at a milling speed of 850 rpm and a depth of cut of 2.5 mm, resulting in a milled part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

On a CNC Turning Center, perform precision turning on a lathed part for 29 minutes using CNC program Program_029A, verified and calibrated tool offsets, and a spindle speed of 1200 rpm, resulting in a finished machined component transferred to a mobile robot.

On the Honing Machine, a surface honing operation is performed on the honed cylinder to achieve precise bore finishing, using a 220 grit honing stone to reach a final bore size of 38.1 mm ± 0.005 mm, and the process runs for 94 minutes, after which the precision finished part is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

Using a punch press, a sheet metal component is subjected to a sheet metal punching operation for 24 minutes, employing a 12.7 mm circular punch at a stroke speed of 120 strokes per minute with die alignment automatically maintained via an optical guide, transforming the input sheet metal on the conveyor belt into a finished cut sheet metal product that is then transferred to a mobile robot.

On the Bandsaw, a metal bar is cut into a lathed part through a bar cutting operation lasting 39 minutes, using a bi-metal variable pitch blade at a saw speed of 60 m/min and producing a 3.2 mm kerf, with the input metal bar fed from a conveyor belt and the resulting lathed part transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Broaching Machine, an internal broaching operation is performed on a lathed part using a pull-type spline broach to achieve IT7 tolerance class, taking 20 minutes, after which the resulting broached component is placed on a ConveyorBelt.

Perform finish milling on a milled part using a horizontal milling machine for 57 minutes at a milling speed of 950 rpm, following a climb milling tool path with a full contour to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 μm, resulting in a finished machined component transferred to a mobile robot.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on sheet metal, using a laser power of 2500 W, a cutting speed of 1.8 m/min, and nitrogen gas assist at 18 bar, for 57 minutes, transforming the input material into cut sheet metal, which is then transferred to the conveyor belt.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs precision wire cutting on the shaped part, using a brass-coated 0.25 mm wire with a peak current of 6 A and a pulse duration of 10 μs at a cutting speed of 4 mm/min, resulting in a precision finished part, and the operation runs for 57 minutes before the output is placed on the ConveyorBelt.

On the Stewart Platform Mills, a multi-axis precision milling operation is performed on the milled part taken from the conveyor belt, using 6-axis synchronized tooling with diamond coating and an active damping system engaged, achieving a milling precision of ±0.005 mm, transforming it into a ground part that is then placed on a mobile robot, all for 86 minutes.

On the Gear Shaper, gear shaping is performed on the broached component to produce a shaped gear, processing for 72 minutes at a shaping speed of 150 strokes per minute to form a 48-tooth spur gear, after which the component is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) machine performs a shearing operation on sheet metal, cutting it into sheared sheet metal using a high-carbon steel, hardened blade at a shear angle of 2 degrees and a cutting speed of 15 strokes per minute, taking 12 minutes to complete, with the input material delivered by a MobileRobot and the finished part transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

Using a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine), a ground part is precision cut through wire EDM cutting in fine finish mode with double pass reverse polarity deburring settings and deionized water as the dielectric fluid, resulting in a precision finished part, and the operation runs for 51 minutes before the output is placed on a conveyor belt.

A milled part is machined on a horizontal milling machine using slot milling with a CNC programmed contour tool path at a milling speed of 950 rpm to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, taking 17 minutes, after which the finished machined component is transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Hobbing Machine, a gear hobbing operation is performed on a broached component loaded from a conveyor belt, using a hobbing speed of 220 rpm and a feed rate of 0.8 mm/rev to produce an involute gear profile with a 20-degree pressure angle, lasting for 32 minutes, resulting in a hobbied gear that is transferred to a mobile robot.

The bandsaw performs a cutting to length operation on a metal bar loaded from a mobile robot, using a bi-metal blade with 4/6 TPI and a saw speed of 60 m/min to achieve a 3 mm kerf, taking 35 minutes to complete, and outputs the resulting lathed part onto a conveyor belt.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs precision wire cutting on a ground part for 6 minutes using fine finish mode for tight tolerances, automatic edge deburring, and deionized water with low conductivity as the dielectric fluid, resulting in a precision finished part transferred to the conveyor belt.

Perform final face milling on a milled part using a horizontal milling machine for 32 minutes, operating at a milling speed of 1200 RPM for high surface accuracy with a climb milling tool path and optimized step-over to achieve a surface finish of 32 microinches Ra, resulting in a finished machined component transferred to a mobile robot.

The Bandsaw performs a bar cutting operation for 10 minutes, using a bi-metal variable pitch blade at a saw speed of 60 feet per minute for alloy steel and a cutting width of 0.045 inches kerf for minimal material loss, to cut a metal bar fed from a MobileRobot into a lathed part that is then placed on a ConveyorBelt.

On the Punch Press, a punching and forming operation is performed on sheet metal for 62 minutes, using a 0.5 inch diameter punch for mounting holes, a stroke speed of 80 strokes per minute for high throughput, and laser-aligned dies to achieve ±0.002 inch accuracy, resulting in a finished sheet metal product that is transferred to a MobileRobot.

On a Horizontal Lathe, a metal bar is subjected to rough turning for 74 minutes using a carbide insert with TNMG 16 04 04 geometry as the cutting tool, rotating the workpiece at 450 RPM for 4140 steel and feeding the tool at a rate of 0.012 inches per revolution, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.
